The single most damaging defect a user hits, because it is silent and it defeats
the loop's last step.

`answer` inserts its option rows with `active = (opt == a.chosen)` — a VERBATIM
STRING EQUALITY between the --chosen text and the --option text (auger.py
cmd_answer, the option insert). Nothing validates the pair, nothing warns, and
the pair is easy to miss because `--option` is naturally a full sentence while
--chosen is naturally a short name for it.

Reproduced verbatim:
  answer --question-id Q-000001 --chosen "The CI box smoke test" \
         --option "CI smoke battery: bunker3 runs the project's own documented
                   smoke check ..." --why-not "..."
  -> D-001 recorded  (confidence -1.0, 1 options, embedded, scope project)
     closed Q-000001
  dump
  -> ACTIVE CONFIGURATION: (nothing active)
     WARNING: decisions with != 1 active option:
       - D-001: 0 of 1 options active — this decision contributes NOTHING

Every subsequent verb inherits the damage: `dump --config` then compares the
hypothesis against a record whose chosen text is not any option, so it reports a
spurious CONTRADICTION ("choosing <option label> contradicts the recorded choice
(<the different sentence>)") for a hypothesis that actually agrees with it.

The documentation invites this: docs/VERBS.md says `--option` is "repeatable —
every alternative, chosen ones included" and `--chosen` is "the choice", with no
statement that the two must be byte-identical.

DELIVERABLE (pick one, but the first two are the fix)
- validate that --chosen resolves to exactly one of the supplied --option values
  before anything is stored, refusing by name otherwise (the resolve_option
  machinery already exists and already refuses loudly); OR
- make --chosen accept an option token (D-001-O3 / O3 / a label) and derive the
  chosen label from the option row, so the two can never disagree; AND
- whatever the mechanism, the success line must state the resulting active-option
  count ("D-001 recorded (1 of 3 options active)"), so an empty configuration can
  never be printed as a clean success.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- `answer --chosen <text not among --option>` exits non-zero naming the mismatch,
  OR is accepted with the chosen option auto-activated — and in either case stores
  exactly one active option
- the recorded decision renders in `dump` with exactly one active option and NO
  spurious contradiction line in `dump --config` for a hypothesis that matches it
- the success line reports the active-option count
- a regression test covers the mismatched-wording case (chosen a sentence, option
  a longer sentence, real use)
- ruff check auger.py clean
